NYB.AI has unveiled Vecura 2.0, an upgraded molecular-discovery platform that it says is designed to bring scientific models, biological data, molecular analysis tools and accelerated computing into one workflow. The Singapore-based start-up is positioning the system as a way to reduce the fragmentation that still slows AI adoption in drug discovery and related life-sciences research. According to the company, the new release moves beyond a simple tool-access layer and towards agentic execution, allowing teams to set objectives, gather context, select models and generate structured recommendations with less manual coordination.
...
The launch builds on Vecura 1.0, which NYB.AI described as a connected environment for compound analysis, target exploration, formulation research, toxicity assessment and translational research. With Vecura 2.0, the company says the platform can now reason across tasks rather than merely respond to prompts. That is meant to make the system closer to how scientists work in practice, where model selection, comparison of outputs and next-step decisions often depend on changing experimental context rather than a single query.
...
NYB.AI is presenting Vecura 2.0 at the NVIDIA Inception Startup Showcase during InnoVEX 2026 in Taipei, with the company seeking feedback from enterprise customers, investors and international buyers. The firm says the platform is intended for use across pharmaceuticals, nutraceuticals, cosmetics, food science, functional ingredients and consumer health. Its broader pitch is that advanced molecular-discovery infrastructure should be more accessible to smaller teams, not only to large pharmaceutical groups and specialist computational labs.

results.snippet: Bringing a new drug to market takes about 10 years. NYB.AI has compressed the front end of that timeline from months to hours with Nebius. The Singapore startup screens billions of compounds to find the few that bind to a disease target. That search rests on molecular docking: modeling how a molecule fits a target protein in 3D. The process is compute-intensive at scale and the accelerated timeline requires rock-solid reliability. That's where Nebius AI Cloud comes in. NYB.AI runs its docking and molecular discovery workloads on Nebius, scaling out to run far more campaigns in parallel than before and leaning on the platform’s stability and reliability to keep long runs moving. “We are very impressed with the cloud platform Nebius has, especially with the scale. We could reduce the compute time from months to a few hours, so we could have feedback loops with scientists in a much faster way.” — Duy Trieu, CTO, NYB.AI We’re proud to support NYB.AI as they speed up the search for new medicines.
